Subject: Initial-packet vs sustained throughput — SLA clarification

Hi Soojin,

Quick clarification as we move toward procurement: our integration team is seeing good average RTs from the Redwood hosted streaming endpoint, but they're concerned about variability on the first packet (time-to-first-token) versus sustained token/sec during longer chats. Our legal and ops teams want explicit language in the SLO that covers: 

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) 95th percentile for streaming (per-utterance)
- Sustained tokens/sec expectations for long-running sessions (10k+ tokens)
- Fallback behavior if streaming degrades (e.g., auto-failover to sync endpoint)

Can you confirm whether these can be firm commitments or whether we need an exception/carveout? If a carveout, please propose the boundary conditions (load, concurrency, model variant) and any monitoring/alerts Atlantic can use.

Thanks,
Daniel

Hi Daniel — thanks for the note and the logs, that helps. Short answer: we can offer a mixed SLA that separates TTFT (streaming) guarantees from sustained throughput commitments, but there are operational caveats we recommend codifying.

High-level proposal (summary):
- TTFT (streaming): 95th percentile <= 250ms for requests under our single-request size threshold (<= 2048 tokens).
- Sustained token/sec: baseline commitment of 15 tokens/sec per stream for sessions > 5k tokens; above that we recommend a staged pilot and capacity reservation.
- Fallback: automatic routing to sync endpoints after a defined degradation window (3 consecutive slow-first-packet events in 1 minute) with a guaranteed sync response SLA (p95 <= 600ms).

Caveats and boundary conditions:
- Guarantees apply to production clusters in the us-west region only (we can extend to eu on request).
- Exceptions allowed during model rollouts, maintenance windows, or sustained overloaded clusters — these should be documented as carveouts with notification windows.

I've attached a short proposal doc that lays out the metrics and an initial monitoring spec. If you prefer, we can propose exact contractual language for your counsel.

Next steps: would you like a one-hour workshop with our infra/product team + Atlantic ops to walk the metrics and a proposed pilot?

Best,

Soojin — quick answers from infra:
- TTFT p95 <=250ms is achievable for requests under 2k tokens on dedicated reserved pools (we measured ~180-210ms p95 on staging with our optimized kernels). On shared host pools under peak multi-tenant load, p95 drifts up to ~320-420ms.
- Sustained token/sec: 15 tokens/sec per stream is achievable if the stream is pinned to a dedicated GPU worker with modest batching (we saw 12–18 tokens/sec depending on model variant and quantization). On shared pools, sustained rates are best-effort.
- Fallback behavior: we can implement automatic routing to sync endpoints; this requires a small client-facing switch and an agreed degradation window.

Telemetry: Ben should expose p95_first_token, sustained_tokens_per_stream (1-min rolling), and a stream-health flag. We can provide a read-only dashboard and webhook alerts for Atlantic.

Recommendation: propose a contractual carveout that:
1) Guarantees TTFT p95 <=250ms for reserved dedicated pools only (list GPUs/region).
2) Commits to sustained tokens/sec for pinned streams under reserved capacity — otherwise label it as "best-effort" and provide monitoring and an SLA-grade pilot.

Marcus
Senior Tech Lead, Inference Runtime

Hi Daniel & Priya — thanks for the patience while we scoped this with infra and legal. Below is our proposed path you can present to procurement: 

Proposed carveout (summary):
- TTFT (streaming) commitment: p95 <= 250ms for single-request sizes <= 2048 tokens, applicable when Atlantic reserves a dedicated pool (region: us-west). This will be a contractual SLO.
- Sustained throughput commitment: 15 tokens/sec per stream guaranteed only for pinned streams running on reserved GPU workers (capacity reservation required). For multi-tenant/shared pools sustained rates are "best-effort" (we will not include a firm tokens/sec number).
- Fallback behavior: on 3 consecutive slow-first-packet events within a 60s window for a given stream, requests will be automatically routed to the sync endpoint with an agreed sync p95 <= 600ms.
- Exceptions: model rollouts, emergency maintenance, or force majeure are carveouts; Redwood will provide 72-hour notice where feasible and a post-incident report for outages affecting SLOs.

Monitoring & access:
- We'll provide a read-only dashboard with p95_first_token, sustained_tokens_per_stream (1-min rolling), and stream_health flags plus webhook alerts.
- Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot on a small reserved pool (4 GPUs) to validate sustained tokens/sec and TTFT at your expected concurrency.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, we can draft contract language for your counsel.
2) I can book a technical workshop with Marcus and Ben to walk the pilot runbook.
3) We'll share a DocuSign powerform for the reserved-pool addendum once procurement confirms capacity size.

Attaching the proposal and a sample streaming_profile CSV with measured staging numbers.
